# Puṇṇakamāṇavapucchā (Snp 5.4 (PTS Snp 199))
**ID:** Snp 5.4 (PTS Snp 199)

**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Puṇṇakamāṇavapucchā* ("The Questions of the Student Puṇṇaka") constitutes the fourth discourse of the *Pārāyanavagga* in the *Suttanipāta*, beginning at verse 1043 [Anderson & Smith 1913; Norman 1997–2001; Saddhatissa 2013; SuttaCentral]. In this dialogue, the young student Puṇṇaka approaches the Buddha with questions [Anderson & Smith 1913; Hazra 1994]. The Buddha explains that ascetics, monarchs (*khattiya*s), and brahmins who offer ritual sacrifices do so out of longing for sensual pleasures and worldly praise; because they are bound to these desires, sacrificial rites cannot enable them to cross beyond birth and old age [Hazra 1994]. Overcoming birth and decay is achieved instead through training the mind to transcend perturbation [SuttaCentral].
Curated passage-level parallels noted in canonical literature include the *Ānandasutta* (AN 3.32) and the *Samādhibhāvanāsutta* (AN 4.41) [SuttaCentral]. The text receives extensive canonical exegesis in the *Cūḷaniddesa*, specifically in the *Puṇṇakamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 7) and the *Pucchā* chapter (Cnd 2), and is further treated in the *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus corroborates these connections, showing 167 Pali-internal matching passages across seven texts—chiefly Cnd 7 (60 matches) and Cnd 2 (20 matches), along with shared formulaic segments in the *Nandamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 11) and the *Nandamāṇavapucchā* (Snp 5.8) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches meeting the threshold are reported [DharmaNexus].
